sequences.name: Human Insulin Signal Fragment (educational)
sequences.description: A short fragment modelled on the start of the human preproinsulin coding region. Contains a clear ATG start codon and a complete open reading frame, so it demonstrates composition, transcription, translation and ORF detection in one sequence.

sequences.name: GC-Rich Synthetic Fragment
sequences.description: A synthetic GC-rich sequence with no stop codons in frame 1. Useful for demonstrating high GC content and an open reading frame that runs off the end of the supplied sequence.

sequences.name: AT-Rich Synthetic Fragment
sequences.description: A short AT-rich sequence with no start codons. Good for demonstrating low GC content and the 'no ORF detected' outcome.

sequences.name: Short Teaching Sequence
sequences.description: A compact 30-base sequence for quick classroom walkthroughs: clean codon structure with a stop codon at the end.

comparisons.name: Reference vs Sample — three point differences
comparisons.description: The same 60-base fragment with two single-base substitutions introduced. Demonstrates the mismatch table, similarity percentage and comparison chart clearly.

comparisons.name: Reference vs Sample — identical sequences
comparisons.description: Two identical sequences, showing a 100% similarity result with an empty mismatch table.

comparisons.name: Reference vs Sample — unequal lengths
comparisons.description: The sample is shorter than the reference, demonstrating how the comparison handles unaligned trailing bases.
